name: Baumkuchen
origin: German for 'tree cake': its concentric rings, visible when sliced, resemble tree growth rings, produced by painting many thin layers of batter onto a rotating spit under a radiant heater, each layer browning before the next is added.

ingredients.note: an unusually egg-rich formula even among sponge cakes, since many yolks and whites, whipped separately, are what let this batter set into dozens of thin layers rather than one thick crumb

process.name: cream butter, sugar and yolks
process.description: beat butter, sugar and egg yolks until pale

process.name: whip whites
process.description: whip egg whites to a stable meringue and fold in

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt

process.name: build layers on the spit
process.description: paint a thin layer of batter onto the rotating spit, brown under the radiant element, then repeat for 15-20 layers

notes: German baking-guild specifications for Baumkuchen call for an unusually high butter and egg content relative to flour, needed for a batter thin enough to paint on and set fast enough under radiant heat to build many distinct layers; figures here are representative of that pattern rather than one single published recipe. The rotating-spit build method is real and is why this is the one cake in the catalogue tagged 'rotary' rather than 'deck' or 'convection'.
